label: Sample Exam Set A
source: ISTQB CTFL v4.0 Sample Exam A, Questions v1.7 / Answers v1.7 (istqb.org)

questions.q: Which of the following statements describe a valid test objective?
o: To prove that there are no unfixed defects in the system under test
To prove that there will be no failures after the implementation of the system into production
To reduce the risk level of the test object and to build confidence in the quality level
To verify that there are no untested combinations of inputs
questions.e: Testing can lower risk and raise confidence in quality, but it can never prove that no defects or failures remain and it cannot test every combination of inputs (testing principles 1, 2 and 7). The other options claim proofs testing cannot deliver.

questions.q: Which of the following options shows an example of test activities that contribute to success?
o: Having testers involved during various software development lifecycle (SDLC) activities will help to detect defects in work products
Testers try not to disturb the developers while coding, so that the developers write better code
Testers collaborating with end users help to improve the quality of defect reports during component integration and system testing
Certified testers will design much better test cases than non-certified testers
questions.e: Early tester involvement raises shared understanding and finds defects in work products as soon as they are created. Isolation does not improve code, end users do not take part in low-level test levels, and a certificate alone does not make a tester better at test design.

questions.q: You have been assigned as a tester to a team producing a new system incrementally. You have noticed that no changes have been made to the existing regression test cases for several iterations and no new regression defects were identified. Your manager is happy, but you are not. Which testing principle explains your skepticism?
questions.e: Repeating the same tests unchanged means they eventually stop finding new defects, the 'tests wear out' principle, so no new regression defects may simply mean the suite is stale.

questions.q: You work in a team that develops a mobile application for food ordering. In the current iteration the team decided to implement the payment functionality. Which of the following activities is a part of test analysis?
o: Estimating that testing the integration with the payment service will take 8 person-days
Deciding that the team should test if it is possible to properly share payment between many users
Using boundary value analysis (BVA) to derive the test data for the test cases that check the correct payment processing for the minimum allowed amount to be paid
Analyzing the discrepancy between the actual result and expected result after executing a test case that checks the process of payment with a credit card, and reporting a defect
questions.e: Defining test conditions, that is what should be tested, is test analysis. Estimating effort is test planning, deriving test data with a technique is test design, and comparing actual with expected results is test execution.

questions.q:
Which of the following factors have a SIGNIFICANT influence on the test approach?
i. The SDLC
ii. The number of defects detected in previous projects
iii. The identified product risks
iv. New regulatory requirements forcing formal white-box testing
v. The test environment setup
o: i, iii, iv have significant influence
ii, iv, v have significant influence
questions.e: The SDLC, the identified product risks and regulatory requirements significantly influence the test approach. Defect numbers from earlier projects have some influence but are not significant, and the test environment setup does not shape the approach.

questions.q: Which TWO of the following tasks belong MAINLY to a testing role?
questions.e: Configuring test environments and analyzing the test basis are testing tasks. The product backlog belongs to the product owner, solution design to developers, and creating the test plan is a managerial responsibility.

questions.q:
Which of the following skills (i-v) are the MOST important skills of a tester?
i. Having domain knowledge
ii. Creating a product vision
iii. Being a good team player
iv. Planning and organizing the work of the team
v. Critical thinking
o: i, iii and v are important
i, ii and v are important
questions.e: Domain knowledge, team work and critical thinking are the core tester skills. Creating a product vision belongs to business roles, and planning and organizing the team's work belongs to the test manager or to the whole team.

questions.q: How is the whole team approach present in the interactions between testers and business representatives?
o: Business representatives decide on test automation approaches
Testers help business representatives to define a test strategy
Business representatives are not part of the whole team approach
Testers help business representatives to create suitable acceptance tests
questions.e: In the whole team approach testers collaborate with business representatives, for example by helping them create suitable acceptance tests. Automation approaches and the test strategy are agreed collaboratively, and business representatives are part of the team.

questions.q: Consider the following rule: 'for every SDLC activity there is a corresponding test activity'. In which SDLC models does this rule hold?
o: Only in iterative and incremental development models
In sequential, incremental, and iterative development models
questions.e: The rule that every SDLC activity has a corresponding test activity holds for all development models, whatever their lifecycle shape.

questions.q: Which of the following statements BEST describes the acceptance test-driven development (ATDD) approach?
o: In ATDD, acceptance criteria are typically created based on the given/when/then format
In ATDD, test cases are mainly created at component testing and are code-oriented
In ATDD, tests are created, based on acceptance criteria to drive the development of the related software
In ATDD, tests are based on the desired behavior of the software, which makes it easier for team members to understand them
questions.e: In ATDD tests are written from acceptance criteria as part of the design process and drive development. The given/when/then style and behaviour focus belong to BDD, and code-oriented component tests describe TDD.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an example of the shift-left approach?
o: Reviewing the user requirements before they are formally accepted by the stakeholders
Writing a component test before the corresponding code is written
Executing a performance efficiency test for a component during component testing
Writing a test script before setting up the configuration management process
questions.e: Test scripts are configuration items, so writing them before configuration management exists is not shift-left. Early reviews, test-first development and early non-functional testing are shift-left practices.

questions.q: Which of the arguments below would you use to convince your manager to organize retrospectives at the end of each release cycle?
o: Retrospectives are very popular these days and clients would appreciate it if we added them to our processes
Organizing retrospectives will save the organization money because without them end user representatives do not provide immediate feedback about the product
Process weaknesses identified during the retrospective can be analyzed and serve as a to do list for the organization's continuous process improvement program
Retrospectives embrace five values including courage and respect, which are crucial to maintain continuous improvement in the organization
questions.e: Retrospectives surface process weaknesses that become the backlog for continuous process improvement. They are internal team events about the process, not client feedback, and courage and respect are Extreme Programming values.

questions.q:
Which types of failures (1-4) fit which test levels (A-D) BEST?
1. Failures in system behavior as it deviates from the user's business needs
2. Failures in communication between components
3. Failures in logic in the code
4. Failures in not correctly implemented business rules
A. Component testing
B. Component integration testing
C. System testing
D. Acceptance testing
questions.e: The test basis decides the level: user business needs are acceptance testing (1D), communication between components is component integration testing (2B), logic in the code is component testing (3A), and business rules are system testing (4C).

questions.q: You are testing a user story with three acceptance criteria: AC1, AC2 and AC3 covered by test cases TC1, TC2 and TC3. Execution 1: TC1 Failed (1), TC2 Passed (2), TC3 Failed (3). Execution 2: TC1 Passed (4), TC2 Failed (5), TC3 Failed (6). Execution 3: TC1 Passed (7), TC2 Passed (8), TC3 Passed (9). Tests are repeated once you are informed that all defects found in the test run are corrected and a new version of the software is available. Which of the above tests are executed as regression tests?
questions.e: Tests 4 and 6 confirm earlier failures, and 8 and 9 confirm the failures of execution 2. Test 5 (TC2) and test 7 (TC1) had passed before, so they are regression tests run to check that a fix did not break working behaviour.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of static testing?
o: Having less expensive defect management due to the ease of detecting defects later in the SDLC
Fixing defects found during static testing is generally much less expensive than fixing defects found during dynamic testing
Finding coding defects that might not have been found by only performing dynamic testing
Detecting gaps and inconsistencies in requirements
questions.e: Defect management does not get cheaper by finding defects later; the later a defect is found, the more expensive it is. The other three statements are genuine benefits of static testing.

questions.q: Which of the following is a benefit of early and frequent feedback?
o: It improves the test process for future projects
It forces customers to prioritize their requirements based on agreed risks
It provides a measure for the quality of changes
questions.e: Early and frequent feedback helps to avoid misunderstandings about requirements. Feedback is not used to prioritize requirements, and it is not a way to measure the quality of changes.

questions.q:
The reviews being used in your organization have the following attributes:
- There is the role of a scribe
- The main purpose is to evaluate quality
- The meeting is led by the author of the work product
- There is individual preparation
- A review report is produced
Which of the following review types is MOST likely being used?
questions.e: A scribe excludes an informal review. Evaluating quality is the main objective of a walkthrough, and the meeting is led by the author, while a moderator leads technical reviews and inspections, so the review is a walkthrough.

questions.q: Which of these statements is NOT a factor that contributes to successful reviews?
o: Participants should dedicate adequate time for the review
Splitting large work products into small parts to make the required effort less intense
Participants should avoid behaviors that might indicate boredom, exasperation, or hostility to other participants
Failures found should be acknowledged, appreciated, and handled objectively
questions.e: Reviews detect defects, not failures, because failures only appear when software is executed. Adequate time, small work products and professional behaviour all contribute to review success.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of experience-based test techniques?
o: Test cases are created based on detailed design information
Items tested within the interface code section are used to measure coverage
The test techniques heavily rely on the tester's knowledge of the software and the business domain
The test cases are used to identify deviations from the requirements
questions.e: Experience-based techniques depend on the tester's knowledge of the software, the domain, likely defects and their distribution. Detailed design and coverage of interface code describe white-box techniques, and checking deviations from requirements describes black-box techniques.

questions.q:
You are testing a simplified apartment search form with only two search criteria:
- floor (ground floor; first floor; second or higher floor)
- garden type (no garden; small garden; large garden)
Each apartment on the ground floor has a garden, apartments on higher floors don't. The form validates that no search criteria violating this rule can be used.
You want to apply equivalence partitioning (EP) to cover each floor and each garden type. What is the minimal number of test cases to achieve 100% EP coverage for valid partitions?
questions.e: 'Small garden' and 'large garden' are only valid with 'ground floor', which takes two tests; two more tests cover 'first floor' and 'second or higher floor', both with 'no garden'. Four test cases cover every valid partition (the syllabus calls this 'each choice' coverage).

questions.q:
You are testing a system that calculates the final course grade: 0-50 failed, 51-60 fair, 61-70 satisfactory, 71-80 good, 81-90 very good, 91-100 excellent.
Your test cases use these final results: TC1 91 (excellent), TC2 50 (failed), TC3 81 (very good), TC4 60 (fair), TC5 70 (satisfactory), TC6 80 (good).
What is the 2-value boundary value analysis (BVA) coverage for the final result achieved with the existing test cases?
questions.e: There are 12 boundary values: 0, 50, 51, 60, 61, 70, 71, 80, 81, 90, 91 and 100. The six test cases cover 50, 60, 70, 80, 81 and 91, that is 6 of 12, so coverage is 50%.

questions.q:
A bicycle rental store introduced a CRM system. Features: anyone can rent a bicycle but members get a 20% discount; if the return deadline is missed the discount is no longer available; after 15 rentals members get a gift T-Shirt.
Decision table conditions: Being a member (T T T T F F F F), Missed deadline (T F T F T F F T), 15th rental (F F T T F F T T). Actions: 20% discount on R2 and R4, Gift T-Shirt on R3, R4 and R8.
Based ONLY on the feature description, which of the above rules describes an impossible situation?
questions.e: R8 combines 'not a member' and 'missed deadline' with a gift T-Shirt, but only members can receive the gift, so R8 cannot happen.

questions.q:
You test a system whose lifecycle is modeled by a state transition diagram. The system starts in INIT and ends in OFF. Transitions: INIT -test-> DEBUG MODE, DEBUG MODE -done-> OFF, INIT -run-> IN OPERATION, IN OPERATION -error-> OFF, IN OPERATION -pause-> ON HOLD, ON HOLD -resume-> IN OPERATION, ON HOLD -done-> OFF.
What is the MINIMAL number of test cases to achieve valid transitions coverage?
questions.e: The 'test' and 'error' transitions cannot occur in one test case and neither can both 'done' transitions, so at least three test cases are needed, for example test-done; run-error-done; run-pause-resume-pause-done.

questions.q: Your test suite achieved 100% statement coverage. What is the consequence of this fact?
o: Each instruction in the code that contains a defect has been executed at least once
Any test suite containing more test cases than your test suite will also achieve 100% statement coverage
Each path in the code has been executed at least once
Every combination of input values has been tested at least once
questions.e: Statement coverage executes every statement, including those containing defects. Coverage does not depend on the number of test cases, loops can make the number of paths unbounded, and exhaustive input testing is impossible.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true for white-box testing?
o: During white-box testing the entire software implementation is considered
White-box coverage metrics can help identify additional tests to increase code coverage
White-box test techniques can be used in static testing
White-box testing can help identify gaps in requirements implementation
questions.e: White-box techniques work from the structure of the test object, not from the requirements, so they cannot reveal missing implementation. They do consider the whole implementation, give objective coverage measures and can be used in reviews.

questions.q: Which of the following BEST describes the concept behind error guessing?
o: Error guessing involves using your knowledge and experience of defects found in the past and typical errors made by developers
Error guessing involves using your personal experience of development and the errors you made as a developer
Error guessing requires you to imagine that you are the user of the test object and to guess errors the user could make interacting with it
Error guessing requires you to rapidly duplicate the development task to identify the sort of errors a developer might make
questions.e: Error guessing is based on the tester's experience of past defects and typical developer errors, often supported by checklists. It is not a usability technique and does not require repeating the development work.

questions.q: There has been a delay in the release of a brand-new application and test execution started late, but you have very detailed domain knowledge and good analytical skills. The full list of requirements has not yet been shared, but management is asking for some test results. Which test technique fits BEST?
questions.e: Exploratory testing is most useful where few specifications exist and time is short, and it uses exactly the domain knowledge and analytical skills described. There is no checklist or defect history yet for error guessing, and branch testing is slow and structural.

questions.q: Which of the following BEST describes the way acceptance criteria can be documented?
o: Performing retrospectives to determine the actual needs of the stakeholders regarding a given user story
Using the given/when/then format to describe an example test condition related to a given user story
Using verbal communication to reduce the risk of misunderstanding the acceptance criteria by others
Documenting risks related to a given user story in a test plan to facilitate the risk-based testing of a given user story
questions.e: Acceptance criteria are typically documented in the given/when/then format as example test conditions of a user story. Retrospectives capture lessons learned, verbal communication documents nothing, and risks are not acceptance criteria.

questions.q:
Consider the user story: As an Editor I want to review content before it is published so that I can ensure the grammar is correct.
Acceptance criteria: the user can log in with the Editor role; the editor can view existing content pages; the editor can edit the page content; the editor can add markup comments; the editor can save changes; the editor can reassign to the content owner role to make updates.
Which is the BEST example of an ATDD test for this user story?
o: Test if the editor can save the document after editing the page content
Test if the content owner can log in and make updates to the content
Test if the editor can schedule the edited content for publication
Test if the editor can reassign to another editor to make updates
questions.e: Option a covers two acceptance criteria at once, editing the page content and saving changes. The others test the content owner's activities, a feature outside the criteria, or a reassignment the criteria do not describe.

questions.q: How do testers add value to iteration and release planning?
o: Testers determine the priority of the user stories to be developed
Testers focus only on the functional aspects of the system to be tested
Testers participate in the detailed risk identification and risk assessment of user stories
Testers guarantee the release of high-quality software through early test design during the release planning
questions.e: Testers add value by taking part in detailed risk identification and risk assessment of user stories. Priorities belong to business representatives with the team, testers cover functional and non-functional aspects, and early test design is not part of release planning.

questions.q: Which TWO of the following options are the exit criteria for testing a system?
o: The ability to log in to the test object by the tester
Requirements are translated into given/when/then format
questions.e: Estimated defect density is a diligence measure and automated regression tests are a completion criterion, so both are exit criteria. Environment readiness, login ability and testable requirements are entry criteria.

questions.q: Your team uses the three-point estimation technique to estimate the test effort for a new high-risk feature: most optimistic 2 person-hours, most likely 11 person-hours, most pessimistic 14 person-hours. What is the final estimate?
questions.e: Three-point estimation: E = (optimistic + 4 x most likely + pessimistic) / 6 = (2 + 44 + 14) / 6 = 10 person-hours.

questions.q:
You test a mobile application for finding nearby restaurants. Test cases, priorities (smaller number is higher priority) and dependencies:
TC 001 Select type of food, priority 3, none
TC 002 Select restaurant, priority 2, TC 001
TC 003 Get direction, priority 1, TC 002
TC 004 Call restaurant, priority 2, TC 002
TC 005 Make reservation, priority 3, TC 002
Which test case should be executed as the third one?
questions.e: TC 001 must run first and TC 002 second to satisfy the dependencies. Of the remaining cases, TC 003 has the highest priority (1), so it runs third.

questions.q:
Map the test categories (1-4) onto the agile testing quadrants (A-D):
1. Usability testing
2. Component testing
3. Functional testing
4. Reliability testing
A. Q1: technology facing, supporting the development team
B. Q2: business facing, supporting the development team
C. Q3: business facing, critique the product
D. Q4: technology facing, critique the product
questions.e: Usability testing is business facing and critiques the product (Q3), component testing is technology facing and supports the team (Q1), functional testing is business facing and supports the team (Q2), and reliability testing is technology facing and critiques the product (Q4).

questions.q:
During a risk analysis a risk was identified: 'Response time is too long to generate a report', likelihood medium, impact high. Response to risk: an independent test team performs performance efficiency testing during system testing; a selected sample of end users performs alpha and beta testing before the release.
What measure is proposed in response to this analyzed risk?
questions.e: Concrete testing actions are planned to lower the likelihood or impact of the risk, which is risk mitigation. The risk is neither accepted, transferred, nor covered by a contingency plan.

questions.q: Which work product can be used by an agile team to show the amount of work that has been completed and the amount of total work remaining for a given iteration?
questions.e: A burndown chart graphs work left against time remaining and is updated daily, so it shows progress continuously within an iteration.

questions.q: You need to update one of the automated test scripts to be in line with a new requirement. Which process indicates that you create a new version of the test script in the test repository?
questions.e: Configuration management provides version control of all test items, including test scripts, so a new script version is a configuration management concern.

questions.q:
A defect report returned as not reproducible reads: 'Application hangs up - 2022-May-03 - John Doe - Rejected. The application hangs up after entering Test input: $a in the Name field on the new user creation screen. Tried to log off and log in with test_admin01, same issue. Tried with other test admin accounts, same issue. No error message received; log (see attached) contains fatal error notification. Based on test case TC-1305, the application should accept the provided input and create the user. Please fix with high priority, this feature is related to REQ-0012, which is a critical new business requirement.'
What critical information is MISSING from this report that would have been useful to the developers?
questions.e: The report never says which environment, build or version of the application was tested, a defect report should name the test item and the test environment. Expected and actual results, references and priority are all present, and the severity information is there.

questions.q: Which test activity does a data preparation tool support?
questions.e: Test design and implementation include identifying, creating or acquiring the testware needed for execution, such as test data. Monitoring and control act on progress, test analysis defines test conditions, and test completion comes too late.

questions.q: Which item correctly identifies a potential risk of performing test automation?
o: It may introduce unknown regressions in production
Sufficient efforts to maintain testware may not be properly allocated
Testing tools and associated testware may not be sufficiently relied upon
It may reduce the time allocated for manual testing
questions.e: The syllabus lists the risk that the effort needed to maintain the testware is underestimated or not allocated. Automation does not introduce regressions in production, tools must be relied upon, and reducing manual testing is the intended benefit.

questions.q: You were given a task to analyze and fix causes of failures in a new system to be released. Which activity are you performing?
questions.e: Debugging finds, analyzes and removes the causes of failures. Testing, requirement elicitation and defect management do not remove causes; they plan, gather requirements or handle defects as work products.

questions.q: In many software organizations the test department is called the Quality Assurance (QA) department. Is this sentence correct or not and why?
o: It is correct. Testing and QA mean exactly the same thing
It is correct. These names can be used interchangeably because both testing and QA focus their activities on the same quality issues
It is not correct. Testing is something more; testing includes all activities with regard to quality. QA focuses on quality-related processes
It is not correct. QA is focused on quality-related processes while testing concentrates on demonstrating that a component or system is fit for purpose and to detect defects
questions.e: Testing and quality assurance are different: QA establishes, monitors and improves quality-related processes, whereas testing plans, prepares and evaluates a test object to show it meets requirements and to detect defects.

questions.q: A phone ringing in a neighboring cubicle distracts a programmer causing him to improperly program the logic that checks the upper boundary of an input variable. Later, during system testing, a tester notices that this input field accepts invalid input values. Which of the following correctly describes an incorrectly coded upper bound?
questions.e: The incorrect code is a defect. The distraction is the root cause, the accepting of invalid input is a failure, and the mistaken thinking that led to the code is an error.

questions.q: Consider this testware: 'Test Charter #04.018, Session time: 1h. Explore: Registration page. With: Different sets of incorrect input data. To discover: Defects related to accepting the registration process with the incorrect input.' Which test activity produces this testware as an output?
questions.e: A test charter is produced by test design, it defines what to explore, with what and to discover what, before test execution starts.

questions.q: Which of the following is the BEST example of how traceability supports testing?
o: Performing the impact analysis of a change will give information about the completion of the tests
Analyzing the traceability between test cases and test results will give information about the estimated level of residual risk
Performing the impact analysis of a change will help selecting the right test cases for regression testing
Analyzing the traceability between the test basis, the test objects and the test cases will help in selecting test data to achieve the assumed coverage of the test object
questions.e: Impact analysis of a change, which relies on traceability between requirements, test cases and results, is what lets a team pick the right test cases for regression testing.

questions.q: Which of the following BEST explains a benefit of independence of testing?
o: The use of an independent test team allows project management to assign responsibility for the quality of the final deliverable to the test team

If a test team external to the organization can be afforded, then there are distinct benefits in terms of this external team not being so easily swayed by the delivery concerns of project management and the need to meet strict delivery deadlines

An independent test team can work separately from the developers, need not be distracted with project requirement changes, and can restrict communication with the developers to defect reporting through the defect management system

When specifications contain ambiguities and inconsistencies, assumptions are made on their interpretation, and an independent tester can be useful in questioning those assumptions and the interpretation made by the developer
questions.e: Specifications are never perfect, so an independent tester is valuable for challenging the assumptions a developer had to make when interpreting them. Quality stays everyone's responsibility and isolation is bad practice.

questions.q: You are working as a tester in the team that follows the V-model. Which of the following activities CAN be performed in the initial phases of the SDLC?
questions.e: In the initial phases of a sequential model, testers can take part in requirement reviews, which is static testing, and can plan and design tests. Dynamic execution, acceptance testing and maintenance testing need a working product.

questions.q:
Which of the following are advantages of DevOps?
i. Faster product release and faster time to market
ii. Increases the need for repetitive manual testing
iii. Constant availability of executable software
iv. Reduction in the number of regression tests associated with code refactoring
v. Setting up the test automation framework is inexpensive since everything is automated
questions.e: DevOps brings faster release and time to market (i) and constant availability of executable software (iii). Manual effort falls rather than rises, more regression tests are needed, and automation frameworks are expensive to set up.

questions.q: One requirement, with high priority, says 'The order must be processed in less than 10 seconds in 95% of the cases'. You created test cases in which a number of random orders were made, the processing time measured, and the results checked against the requirement. What test type did you perform?
o: Functional, because the test cases cover the user's business requirement for the system
Non-functional, because they measure the system's performance
Functional, because the test cases interact with the user interface
White-box, because we need to know the internal structure of the program to measure the order processing time
questions.e: Measuring how fast orders are processed tests performance efficiency, a non-functional test type. Business priority and a user interface do not make a test functional, and no structural knowledge is needed.

questions.q: Your organization's test strategy suggests that once a system is going to be retired, data migration shall be tested. As part of what test type is this testing MOST likely to be performed?
questions.e: Testing data migration when a system is retired is maintenance testing, which covers modifications and retirement. Regression, reliability and integration testing address other objectives.

questions.q:
Which of these work products can be reviewed?
i. Business requirements
ii. Schedule
iii. Test budget
iv. Third-party executable code
v. User stories and their acceptance criteria
o: i and iv can be reviewed
i, ii, iii and iv can be reviewed
i, ii, iii, and v can be reviewed
iii, iv, v can be reviewed
questions.e: Almost any work product can be reviewed, but third-party executable code cannot be read into, so requirements, the schedule, the budget and user stories with acceptance criteria can be reviewed.

questions.q:
Decide which of the following statements (i-v) are true for static testing.
i. Abnormal external behaviors are easier to identify with this testing
ii. Discrepancies from a coding standard are easier to find with this testing
iii. It identifies failures caused by defects when the software is run
iv. Its test objective is to identify defects as early as possible
v. Missing coverage for critical security requirements is easier to find and fix
o: i, iv, v are true for static testing
i, iii, iv are true for static testing
ii, iii are true for static testing
ii, iv, v are true for static testing
questions.e: Static testing finds violations of standards (ii), seeks defects as early as possible (iv) and reveals traceability or coverage gaps in the test basis (v). Abnormal external behaviour and failures require executing the software.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about formal reviews is TRUE?
o: Some reviews do not require more than one role
The review process has several activities
Documentation to be reviewed is not distributed before the review meeting, with the exception of the work product for specific review types
Defects found during the review are not reported since they are not found by dynamic testing
questions.e: A review follows several activities such as planning, initiation, individual review, communication and analysis, fixing and reporting. Every review type has more than one role, work products are distributed early, and defects found are reported.

questions.q: What task may management take on during a formal review?
o: Taking overall responsibility for the review
Deciding what is to be reviewed
Ensuring the effective running of review meetings, and moderating, if necessary
Recording review information such as review decisions
questions.e: Management decides what is to be reviewed. Taking overall responsibility for the review is the review leader's task, moderating meetings belongs to the moderator, and recording information belongs to the scribe.

questions.q:
A wine storage system measures the wine cell temperature T in degrees Celsius, rounded to the nearest degree, and alarms if T deviates from the optimal value of 12: T = 12 gives 'optimal temperature', T < 12 gives 'temperature is too low!', T > 12 gives 'temperature is too high!'.
You want to use the 3-point boundary value analysis (BVA) to verify the behavior of the control device. A test input is a temperature in degrees Celsius. What is the MINIMAL set of test inputs that achieves 100% of the desired coverage?
questions.e: There are four boundaries, 10/11, 11/12, 12/13 and 13/14, and 3-point BVA tests each boundary with both neighbours, which needs 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about branch testing is CORRECT?
o: If a program includes only unconditional branches, then 100% branch coverage can be achieved without executing any test cases
If the test cases exercise all unconditional branches in the code, then 100% branch coverage is achieved
If 100% statement coverage is achieved, then 100% branch coverage is also achieved
If 100% branch coverage is achieved, then all decision outcomes in each decision statement in the code are exercised
questions.e: Each decision outcome corresponds to a conditional branch, so 100% branch coverage exercises every decision outcome. Branch coverage implies statement coverage, not the other way round, and unconditional branches do not give coverage.

questions.q: You are testing a mobile banking application, running a test suite that evaluates each screen and each field against a general list of user interface best practices taken from a popular book on maximizing usability. Which option BEST categorizes the test technique you are using?
questions.e: The list of best practices is a checklist of test conditions to be checked systematically, which makes this checklist-based testing.

questions.q: Which of the following BEST describe the collaborative approach to user story writing?
o: User stories are created by testers and developers and then accepted by business representatives
User stories are created by business representatives, developers, and testers together
User stories are created by business representatives and verified by developers and testers
User stories are created in a way that they are independent, negotiable, valuable, estimable, small, and testable
questions.e: Collaborative story writing means business representatives, developers and testers create the stories together to reach a shared vision. Option d lists the INVEST properties, not the collaboration approach.

questions.q: A test plan contains: 'Testing will be performed using component testing and component integration testing. The regulations require to demonstrate that 100% branch coverage is achieved for each component classified as critical.' Which part of the test plan does this belong to?
questions.e: Test levels, coverage criteria and regulatory constraints on how testing is done all belong to the test approach section of a test plan.

questions.q: Your team uses planning poker to estimate test effort. The team rule says that if there is no time to reach full agreement and the variation in results is small, rules like 'accept the number with the most votes' can be applied. After two rounds there was no consensus, so a third round was run. Round 3 estimates were 13, 8, 13, 13, 13, 13, 8. Which is the BEST next step?
o: The product owner has to step in and make a final decision
Accept 13 as the final test estimate as this has most of the votes
No further action is needed. Consensus has been reached
Remove the new feature from the current release because consensus has not been reached
questions.e: The variation (8, 13) is small and 13 has the most votes, which is exactly when the team rule applies, so 13 is accepted.

questions.q: Which of the following is TRUE regarding the test pyramid?
o: It emphasizes having far more tests at the lower test levels
It suggests that each low-level test checks a large part of the functionality
It describes distribution of test types across the SDLC
It has no impact on the construction of automated tests
questions.e: The test pyramid shows that the number of tests should be largest at the lowest levels and smallest at the top, where each low-level test checks a small, focused piece of logic. It guides automation.

questions.q: During risk analysis the team considered the risk 'The system allows too high a discount for a customer' and estimated the risk impact to be very high. What can one say about the risk likelihood?
o: It is also very high. High risk impact always implies high risk likelihood
It is very low. High risk impact always implies low risk likelihood
One cannot say anything about risk likelihood. Risk impact and risk likelihood are independent
Risk likelihood is not important with such a high-risk impact. One does not need to define it
questions.e: Impact and likelihood are independent factors and both are needed to determine the risk level, so nothing can be concluded about likelihood from impact alone.

questions.q:
Which of these identified risks are project risks?
i. Management moves two experienced testers to another project
ii. The system does not comply with security standards
iii. System response time exceeds user requirements
iv. Stakeholders have inaccurate expectations
v. Disabled people have problems when using the system
questions.e: Project risks concern the management of the project, such as losing staff (i) or unclear stakeholder expectations (iv). The others are product risks about the quality of the test object.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of how product risk analysis influences thoroughness and scope of testing?
o: The test manager monitors and reports the level of all known risks on a daily basis so the stakeholders can make an informed decision on the release date
One of the identified risks was 'Lack of support of open-source databases', so the team decided to integrate the system with an open-source database
During the quantitative risk analysis, the team estimated the total level of all identified risks and reported it as the total residual risk before testing
Risk assessment revealed a very high level of performance risks, so it was decided to perform detailed performance efficiency testing early in the SDLC
questions.e: Choosing detailed performance efficiency testing early because of a high performance risk shows risk analysis shaping the thoroughness and timing of testing. The others are monitoring, an architectural decision and a quantitative analysis.

questions.q: Which TWO of the following options are common metrics used for reporting on the quality level of the test object?
o: Number of defects found during system testing
Total effort on test design divided by the number of designed test cases
Number of defects found divided by the size of a work product
Time needed to repair a defect
questions.e: The number of defects found and defect density (defects divided by the size of the work product) relate to the quality of the test object. Effort per test case, executed procedures and time to repair are process metrics.

questions.q: Which of the following pieces of information contained in a test progress report is the LEAST useful for business representatives?
o: New risks within the test cycle
questions.e: Branch coverage is a technical metric used by developers and technical test analysts, so it means little to business representatives. Impediments, progress and new risks all matter to them.
